UPSTREAM: commonlib: update fsp_relocate to make it compatible with UEFI 2.6 UEFI 2.6 spec casts the return of FFS_FILE2_SIZE to a UINT32 which cannot be read using read_le32(&returnval). CHROMIUM: iwl7000: mac80211: linearize RX frame before extracting 802.3s The upstream version of cfg80211 (i.e. >= v4.7) now supports paging in the skbuff when extracting 802.3 packets from an AMSDU. The mac80211 code delivered with iwl7000 followed upstream, where the linearization is not needed anymore. But chromeos's vesion of cfg80211 doesn't have this change yet, so mac80211 still needs to linearize before passing the buffer to cfg80211. BUG=chrome-os-partner:57003 TEST=connect to an AP (e.g. OnHub) that sends several AMPDUs embedded in an AMSDU. UPSTREAM: cpufreq: Fix GOV_LIMITS handling for the userspace governor Currently, the userspace governor only updates frequency on GOV_LIMITS if policy->cur falls outside policy->{min/max}. However, it is also necessary to update current frequency on GOV_LIMITS to match the user requested value if it can be achieved within the new policy->{max/min}. This was previously the behaviour in the governor until commit d1922f0 ("cpufreq: Simplify userspace governor") which incorrectly assumed that policy->cur == user requested frequency via scaling_setspeed. This won't be true if the user requested frequency falls outside policy->{min/max}. Ex: a temporary thermal cap throttled the user requested frequency. Fix this by storing the user requested frequency in a seperate variable. The governor will then try to achieve this request on every GOV_LIMITS change. Fixes: d1922f02562f (cpufreq: Simplify userspace governor) Signed-off-by: Sai Gurrappadi <sgurrappadi@nvidia.com> Acked-by: Viresh Kumar <viresh.kumar@linaro.org> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit e43e94c1eda76dabd686ddf6f7825f54d747b310) BUG=chrome-os-partner:56913 TEST= On kevin, run: cd /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq echo userspace > scaling_governor cd /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu4/cpufreq echo userspace > scaling_governor cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_max_freq > \ /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_setspeed cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu4/cpufreq/scaling_max_freq > \ /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu4/cpufreq/scaling_setspeed . Check current speed and confirm fastest: . grep . /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu[04]/cpufreq/cpuinfo_cur_freq . Get device hot. Check speed and confirm throttled: . grep . /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu[04]/cpufreq/cpuinfo_cur_freq . Let device cool down and check that the speed is fastest again: . grep . /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu[04]/cpufreq/cpuinfo_cur_freq Change-Id: I26d8c3ac3ae5a7124275746036fec36b444e1686 Signed-off-by: Javi Merino <javi.merino@arm.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/381471 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Tested-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>
